page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz with AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI instruction sets. It employs a constrained core topology offering 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with multithreading. Memory allocation totals 128 GB of RAM, providing an expansive 32 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 945 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Discrete GPUs are not present in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier single-core CPU throughput, with stress-ng single-core performance and single-threaded gzip compression both placing in the top 10% tier. Because total core capacity is restricted to 4 vCPUs, aggregate parallel throughput is moderate; stress-ng multi-core results position in the middle 50%, while multithreaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25%. Memory subsystem throughput remains consistent across tests, recording 48.62 GB/s uncached read bandwidth and 34.0 GB/s write bandwidth. Application benchmarks demonstrate 7.7 million Redis SET operations per second and 8.76 GB/s static web serving throughput.

The hardware configuration is engineered for workloads requiring substantial RAM allocations and low-latency local scratch storage without consuming excessive CPU cores. By providing 32 GB RAM per vCPU, the instance yields strong qualitative cost efficiency for environments constrained by per-core software licensing fees. Tradeoffs include limited compute parallelism, rendering it less suitable for high-throughput batch compilation or large machine learning inference. Recommended workloads include relational database management systems, Redis caching clusters, ETL pipelines, and in-memory analytical engines.

The configuration pairs 128 GB of RAM with 945 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, achieving an expansive 32 GB of memory per vCPU without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compute and compression speeds, though total parallel throughput remains moderate due to the 4-vCPU limit. Memory bandwidth and operations like Redis SET transactions perform at consistent median levels. This architecture delivers qualitative cost efficiency for systems bound by per-core software licensing costs that simultaneously require large memory working sets. Recommended workloads encompass relational database management systems, in-memory caching platforms, and data analytics processes needing local high-speed temporary storage.
